description: Change the contact activate flag for existing contacts. When set to 'on' (true), the activate flag ensures the contact remains in an active state until automatically deleted by the contact detection system, and also sets the inhibit flag to false. When set to 'off' (false), contact activity is determined by the contact model. By default, only mechanical contacts are considered. The activate flag is off by default.

parameters.flag: True to activate (always active), False to deactivate (model-determined)

methods.returns: True if contact is activated (activate flag is on)

methods.description: Get the contact activity state (current active/inactive status)
methods.returns: True if contact is currently active
notes: Different from activated() - active() returns current state, activated() returns flag value
Python SDK requires iteration over contacts - cannot activate all contacts in one call
Command interface is more efficient for bulk activation
Use range specification in command interface to avoid Python iteration
Three related methods: activate() (setter), activated() (getter for flag), active() (getter for current state)

6.0: Live 6.0 grammar: the optional process selector precedes the subcommand ('contact mechanical <sub>' / 'contact thermal <sub>'); it is not a keyword of the subcommand itself.
7.0: Live 7.0 grammar: the optional process selector precedes the subcommand ('contact mechanical <sub>' / 'contact thermal <sub>'); it is not a keyword of the subcommand itself.
9.0: Live 9.7 grammar: the optional process selector precedes the subcommand ('contact mechanical <sub>' / 'contact thermal <sub>' / 'contact fluid <sub>' - fluid is 9.x-new); it is not a keyword of the subcommand itself.

examples.description: Activate all contacts - they remain active until deleted by contact detection system. Use case: Ensure all contacts stay active regardless of contact model logic.
Deactivate all contacts - activity determined by contact model. Use case: Return to default behavior where contact model controls activity.
Activate contacts in 'specimen' group only. Use case: Selective activation of specific contact subset.

examples.command: contact activate false range contact type 'ball-facet'
examples.description: Deactivate ball-facet contacts, let model determine activity. Use case: Allow contact model to control ball-facet contact activity.

examples.command: contact activate on mechanical range contact
examples.description: Explicitly activate all mechanical contacts. Use case: When working with multiple contact processes.

examples.command: contact activate true range model null
examples.description: Activate contacts with null model (forces them to stay in system). Use case: Keep null contacts in system even though they transmit no forces.
